sourceInformation.source: H.E.R.O. (Activision, 1984), created by John Van Ryzin
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, Web Audio API, Gamepad API, WebRTC; AI Hub session client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural low-poly cave dioramas, cel shading, ink edges, teal crystal light and amber rescue equipment
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js native AnimationMixer and AnimationClip tracks for rotor, walking, wing flaps and miner waves; procedural secondary motion and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated synth music at 10% default, rotor/laser/dynamite/cave effects and formant-filtered Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world authoritative co-op for 1–2 operators; standalone direct WebRTC invite/answer co-op; local shared-screen co-op
sourceInformation.testing: 208 automated checks covered: 47 real-Rapier simulation checks, 19 UI checks, 48 audio/transport/protocol checks, 43 bundled-game checks, 46 full-game AI Hub checks and 5 package checks. Scripted physical campaign uses developer survival assistance; gamepad and touch are emulated. Visual review used WebGL 2 because headless WebGPU screenshots were blank.
sourceInformation.research: Original Activision manual scan and archive screenshot, manual transcription, Atarimania and Games Database descriptions; original sound vocabulary researched, exact waveform fidelity unknown; official AI Hub docs and Three.js r180 source

testingFeedback: 21 implementation or integration issues found across automated tests and code/visual review; all fixed. Test-script assumptions were tracked separately.
7 critical boot, multiplayer progression, or session-lifecycle issues; all fixed.
The input-driven five-mission physical campaign playthrough and two-browser assignment-transition test, backed by the official impaired-network AI Hub harness.
Standalone syntax checks; they could not reveal browser initialization, focus, physics reachability, or multiplayer lifecycle failures.
engineFeedback: Three.js made original 3D cutaway art and native animation tracks straightforward, and Rapier supplied reliable collision and moving platforms.

Two boot mistakes surfaced in the packaged browser test: script replacement corrupted dollar patterns and a resize method was missing. Both were fixed. WebGPU screenshots on this headless adapter were blank; state checks and WebGL 2 visual review verified the game.
The complete rescue simulation, authored missions, controller menu navigation, procedural sound, and authoritative network synchronization.
Keeping render state, fixed-step physics, guest snapshots, and menu transitions coherent across standalone and AI Hub play.
none; the engine and physics dependencies are unmodified.
More predictable headless WebGPU screenshot readback and a compact official cel-shading example would help.
promptFeedback: The clear source, controller-first design, attract-mode requirement and single-file deliverable gave the game a strong identity.
The source name does not specify an original platform; the Atari 2600 original was selected, with manual details cross-checked across ports.
Completing and validating the full campaign, procedural presentation, and two different multiplayer launch paths in one portable file.
Specify the preferred original platform and whether standalone Internet co-op may depend on a hosted signaling service.

aiHub.name: H.E.R.O. IN A HOLE
aiHub.tagline: The deep end of the day job.
aiHub.description: Clock in for five volcanic cave rescues with a rotor pack, helmet laser and six sticks of dynamite. Bring fifteen miners home solo or with a workmate in local or online co-op.
aiHub.controls: WASD/left stick move, Space/× fly, mouse/right stick aim, LMB/J/R2 laser, E/□ dynamite, Esc/Options pause; P2 arrows/N/M; touch drag controls.
